rule.text: At least 12 credits of upper-division work in chemistry must be taken at Stony Brook; these must be taken in at least two of the major subdisciplines (inorganic, physical, and organic chemistry).
rule.reason: Program-wide residency rule over upper-division chemistry credits across subdisciplines; no rule type covers this.

requirements.sourceText: At least 12 credits of upper-division work in chemistry must be taken at Stony Brook; these must be taken in at least two of the major subdisciplines (inorganic, physical, and organic chemistry).

policies.sourceText: All of the courses used to fulfill the requirements of the major (CHE, MAT, ESG, PHY, etc.) must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher, with the exception of three courses, for which the grade may be C-. G/P/NC grades are not acceptable in courses taken for the major.

All of the courses used to fulfill the requirements of the major (CHE, MAT, ESG, PHY, etc.) must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher, with the exception of three courses, for which the grade may be C-. No transferred course with a grade lower than C may be used to fulfill any major requirement.

fulfillment.sourceText: Each student majoring in Chemistry must use CHE 303, CHE 304, or CHE 384 to satisfy the writing requirement for the Chemistry major (a satisfactory grade is required).

notes.text: Three courses in the major may be passed with a grade of C-. The page does not identify which three courses, so this exception is not modeled.
The sample sequence marks CHE 304 and CHE 328 with ** and states that only one of these two laboratory courses is required.

The Bachelor of Science program, its options (biological chemistry, chemical physics, environmental chemistry, chemical science), and the Chemistry Honors Program are not modeled. The honors program requires a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 in science and mathematics through the junior year, a senior thesis, and a 3.40 GPA in senior-year chemistry courses.
The Chemistry Secondary Teacher Education Program is described under the Education and Teacher Certification entry and is not modeled here.
Minors of particular interest to Chemistry majors are Biology (BIO), Environmental Studies (ENS), and Marine Sciences (MAR).
Students interested in combining chemistry with materials science should see the Interdisciplinary Program: Engineering Chemistry, BS.
